2. The appellant in this case is seeking suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

He has been convicted vide judgment dated 05.12.2024 and sentenced vide order dated 16.12.2024 in POCSO Case No. 2275/2014, arising out of Islampur P.S. Case No.

sentences.text: The prosecution case is based on a written information submitted by the father of the victim girl who alleged that his daughter (X) used to come to his house where he was residing every night with the food.

He has stated that for last six months the appellant used to take the daughter of the informant to nearby Mahadev Sthal and commit rape on her, which was informed to the informant by his daughter after a long time as she did not disclose it due to some social stigmas.
The informant claimed that few days earlier, his daughter has disclosed about the commission of rape by the appellant.

Whereafter he had gone to the place of the appellant to enquire about it, he had beaten him whereafter the informant lodged the case, but in the said case because of the social stigma that has to be attached, he had suppressed about the commission of rape Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.105 of 2025(3) dt.03-09-2025 on his daughter.
On the basis of the written information (Exhibit-01), the FIR was lodged on 03.11.2014.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in course of the trial the victim-girl was examined as P.W.-
5.
She has stated that the occurrence had taken place about 3 years ago when she was returning at 08:00 P.M. after serving meal to her father.
This appellant had taken her to khatihan where he had committed rape on her and thrust her oodhni into her mouth.
P.W.-5 has stated that she had come back to her house and told the occurrence to her father.

It is, thus pointed out that the victim had informed about the occurrence immediately after reaching her house, but the informant has stated in his written information that only few days back, she had informed about the occurrence.
5.
Learned counsel further submits that P.W.-5 has stated that after two months of the said occurrence, her father had gone to the police station to lodge the case.
He had lodged the case only of marpeet and had not lodged the case of rape due to social stigma but, when the accused was again teasing her, her father lodged a case of rape.

It is submitted that the victim P.W.-5 has not stated about any Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.105 of 2025(3) dt.03-09-2025 subsequent occurrence of commission of rape on her and she has clearly stated that because the accused was repeatedly teasing her, therefore, her father has lodged the case of rape.

6. Learned counsel points out that P.W.-5 has admitted in her deposition that before police in her statement she had not stated that the appellant had caught hold of her and took her to khatihan and committed rape on her.
7. Learned counsel further submits that in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the learned Magistrate also the victim-P.W.5 had not stated that she was subject to continuous rape.

It is evident from her statement that in the FIR lodged earlier by her father, it was a simple case of marpeet but, later on a case of rape was lodged against the appellant because as per her statement,
he was indulged in teasing her.
8.
Learned counsel further submits that the I.O. of the case has stated that he had not found any sign of trampled straws at the place of occurrence.
The victim had not produced her clothes and when the victim had come to Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.105 of 2025(3) dt.03-09-2025 him, he had not found any stains on her clothes.

The I.O. has also stated that the when the victim Uday Mahto @ Uday Prasad vs The State Of Bihar on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11319114/
2 came to him for the first time, he had not found any injury on her head, legs, back or cheek.
9.

sentences.text: The doctor has found her age between 17 and 18 years and it is opined that she was habitual to sexual intercourse.
There was no evidence of recent intercourse.

It is thus, submitted that the whole prosecution case is based on the testimony of the prosecutrix who has not supported the prosecution case of rape in course of investigation before the I.O.
10.
The prayer of the appellant has been opposed by learned counsel for the informant and learned A.P.P. for the State.

It is submitted that in the written information submitted by the father of the victim, he has stated that the victim was being continuously raped near Mahadev Sthan and this fact was told to him few days ago by his daughter.

It is further not controverted that in her own statement in trial, the victim has stated that before the I.O. she had not stated about commission of rape by the appellant and the place of occurrence as given by her in her testimony is Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.105 of 2025(3) dt.03-09-2025 different from that of one stated by her father in his written information.

11. Having regard to the submissions noted hereinabove and the materials which we have prima facie gone through, at this stage noticing that the place of occurrence, date of occurrence as disclosed in the written information are not being supported by the victim (P.W.5), the I.O. did not find any sign of trampled straws at the place of occurrence, nor had he noticed any injury and the doctor has not opined commission of recent sexual act, the delay in lodging of the FIR for over two months and the statement of the victim that indicates that her father had lodged the rape case because the appellant was repeatedly teasing her are some of the reasons which constitute sufficient grounds to allow the appellant to be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 7 th Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act,
Nalanda at Bihar Sharif in connection with POCSO Case No. 2275/2014 arising out of Islampur P.S.
Case No. Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.105 of 2025(3) dt.03-09-2025 309/2014.
